body:
Hi Tim,

Thank you for flagging these discrepancies. Digging into our pipeline from 4 years ago, here's what I think happened:

1. ESM1b vs EVE: The code that created the main text and Fig. 2b (36,537 ClinVar and 30,497 HGMD/gnomAD variants) was supposed to be identical to the code used for Supplementary Table 2 and Fig. 2e-h (36,522 and 30,483 variants), but apparently there were minor differences we failed to notice (e.g. a handful of protein sequences mapped differently). The differences in final metrics are insubstantial (ROC-AUC difference <= 0.002). I recommend taking the numbers from Supplementary Table 2, which reflect the released version of the benchmark ([benchmarks/ClinVar_gnomAD_benchmark_with_predictions.csv](https://github.com/ntranoslab/esm-variants/blob/main/benchmarks/ClinVar_gnomAD_benchmark_with_predictions.csv)).
 
2. Stop-gains: There seems to have been a similar minor error. The Methods counts (32,441 NMD and 36,113 pathogenic overall) are the ones used in the analysis. The difference is likely 79 pathogenic variants whose stop codon falls right at the 50 bp boundary. We grouped them with the NMD variants, but they were left out of the counts in the Fig. 6d legend and the Supplementary Methods. Excluding them changes ESM1b's NMD ROC-AUC only very slightly (0.5658 to 0.5664). And yes, the values in Table_of_results_stop_gains are ROC-AUCs over the whole set (as reported in the text), while Fig. 6d plots means over 20 bootstrap draws.

I apologize for the mistakes.

Best,
Nadav
